title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 182
text:
39. Adjustments may involve:
• Proceeding at a slower pace.
• Speaking to a witness through a signer or an interpreter.

40. In more severe cases, there is scope for:
• Appointing an intermediary to assist with communication (in criminal, family or other
courts where intermediaries are used).

41. Where there is additionally a mental disability, see the parallel section in chapter 4 (Mental
disability). On this topic, it is useful to read the sections on “Adjustments to
cross-examination” and “Questioning techniques to avoid” in relation to vulnerable witnesses
in chapter 2 (Children, young people and vulnerable adults).
Representation

42. Guidance on McKenzie Friends and lay representatives is in chapter 1.

43. To meet the needs of a disabled party, a judge may facilitate representation in a form which
might not otherwise have been permitted. For instance, lay representation.
